item.title: Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center Names Artists in Residence for 2023-2024
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Contact: Dominique Shank, Columbus Recreation and Parks Department, 614-512-0049 (cell)


Sept. 13, 2023

Columbus, Ohio – The Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center today announced it has selected Max Adrian and Grace Johnson as the Artists in Residence for 2023-2024. Adrian will serve his residency from October 2023 to January 2024, while Johnson will serve her residency from February 2024 to May 2024.

Max Adrian is a textile-based artist who creates soft sculptures, quilts and inflatables using materials such as faux fur, nylon, ripstop, spandex and vinyl. His artwork draws on themes of queerness, desire and consumer culture. Adrian’s pieces include references to various topics ranging from pet furniture to drag queens. Originally from Kansas City, MO, he graduated from the Kansas City Art Institute in 2015 with a Bachelor's Degree in Fine Arts before earning a Master of Fine Arts in Fiber and Material Studies from the Tyler School of Art and Architecture in Philadelphia. Adrian’s professional experience includes puppetry and performance design. Since 2016 he has been based out of Columbus.

Grace Johnson is a Columbus native who creates cloth-print pieces using plant and dye material. Often, she sources organic materials from right here in central Ohio. Finding her materials may include using foliage from Westgate Park or repurposing leftover flower arrangements. With each piece, Johnson hopes to tell a story that creates an essence of a particular time, place or feeling. Her experience includes working for the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Refugees (UNCHR) in Southeast Asia and Central America during the 1980s. Upon returning to Columbus, she worked at The Ohio State University, where she served as the Director of International Programs and later as the Chief of Staff at the Office of Diversity and Inclusion. 

Launched in 2021 by Columbus Recreation and Parks Department and the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center, the Artist in Residence program fosters engagement with the local community by providing opportunities for creatives in the city, with the aim of building a diverse network of local artists. Two participants are chosen annually by an independent panel of six, made up of a combination of community members and artists. Those who are selected as the Artists in Residence receive access to studio space, along with organizational and material support, as well as a stipend and a platform to present artwork created during their residency.

To learn more about the Artist in Residence program as well as the exhibitions, classes and opportunities the Priscilla R. Tyson Cultural Arts Center has to offer, visit CulturalArtsCenterOnline.org.

item.title: The Earth is US: Forging a New Relationship
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

The Columbus Cultural Arts Center invites you to its major exhibition of the year, The Earth is US: Forging a New Relationship, which runs from Sept. 16 through Oct. 29. The event also features an opening reception on Friday, Sept. 16, from 6 to 8 p.m.

In our modern, engineered lives, we’ve lost touch with the rhythms of the natural world which keeps us alive. Participating artists draw from the wisdom of both ancient peoples and modern science to bring about a deeper understanding of the importance of environmental stewardship. Through art and science, the exhibition seeks to show how what happens within the ground beneath our feet, in the water we drink, and in the air we breathe, is mirrored within our own bodies. There can be no deeper connection. A healthy planet is essential for our own health and well-being.

Join the Cultural Arts Center and its artists, and share your thoughts on what we as humans must do to secure a livable future for our children and grandchildren. 

We look forward to seeing you,

Geoffrey A. Martin
Arts Administrator

Exhibition events include:

Friday, Sept. 16, 6-8 p.m. | Free, Opening Reception

Friday, Sept. 30, 7 p.m. | Free, Panel Discussion: Forging a New Relationship

Friday, Oct. 14, 7 p.m.* | Free, Special performance featuring musicians from the Columbus Symphony Orchestra, readers from the Ohio Poetry Association and dancers from Global Water Dance Columbus.

*Special location for this event: Columbus Performing Arts Center, 549 Franklin Ave.

Details about workshops associated with the exhibition can be found on the Cultural Arts Center’s web page.

item.title: Cultural Arts Center Happenings! - November Newsletter
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

November Newsletter

Coming Up in the Cultural Art Center Galleries...

We have arrived at our final exhibition line up of 2021!

Join us on Friday, November 19th from 6-8PM as we celebrate artists Brian Riegel and Steven Riggs! Riegel will be exhibiting the body of work Out of Tunes in our Main Gallery, while Riggs will be exhibiting THE HUMAN FACTOR in our Loft Gallery. 

 

Riegel takes reclaimed musical instruments and morphs them into fantastical mixed media sculptures. Many of theses instruments are Steampunk/Dieselpunk inspired, and are bound to make you wonder what you might create from that old clarinet or trumpet that’s been hiding in the back of your closet.

 

Riggs combines old world techniques with oils and graphite in order to create portraits, landscapes, and mythological scenes. Each work is a combination of past experiences, with an intense study of literature and history.

 

These are sure to be stellar exhibitions! Be on the look out for Instagram LIVE tours, Conversations and Coffee virtual talks, and more exciting content coming up in the last few weeks of the year! 

Let's Shop Till We Drop!

The holiday season is officially here friends!

 

What better way to shop for those on your list than by visiting two fantastic gift shops with unique works of art and handmade wares right here in downtown Columbus? 

 

First up, located right inside the Cultural Arts Center, Created offers shoppers the chance to peruse our unbelievable line up of works created by our very own CAC teachers and students! Everything from ceramics to enamel works, cards to handcrafted jewelry, there is truly something for everyone on your list. 

 

Head up the road to the Golden Hobby Gift Shop, and you will quickly discover a huge variety of handmade works created by local seniors! Here you can explore a wide selection of unique, handcrafted goods - from inspiring art to clever household items, one of a kind jewelry to fashionable accessories, Golden Hobby has something for everyone! 

 

Created is open during the Cultural Arts Center's normal business hours: Mon. 1-4PM & 7-10PM, Tue.-Thurs. 9-4PM & 7-10PM, and Fri./Sat. 9-4PM (Sundays closed). You can also shop at our virtual store any time here! 

Golden Hobby Gift Shop is open Tues-Saturday 10AM-4:30PM and Sundays from 1-4PM. 

 

Get those lists organized, and come visit the shops today! 

Brianna Rhodes' Keeps Us Dancing, and More Artist in Residence 2022-2023 News Coming Soon!

Dayton, Ohio native and dancer Brianna Rhodes has delivered non-stop amazing classes for the last two months while participating as our Fall/Winter Artist in Residence! From Afrobeat to Modern, Heels to Hip-Hop, Rhodes' has covered a wide range of movement for students participating in any of her fiery workshops. Want to see and learn more about Rhodes? Visit our website! Want to catch a glimpse of Rhodes and her students at work? Watch a blazing hip hop routine here!

 

And stay tuned - we will be unveiling more application information in the coming weeks for our 2022-2023 Artist in Residence program! Visit our website today to learn more!

Do You Take Your Coffee Black, with Cream, or Virtual?

The year may be coming to a close, but we still have plenty of Conversation and Coffee brewing!

 

November 18th @ 12PM: Brian Riegel, Main Gallery artist, joins the conversation to tell us more about the mixed media exhibition Out of Tunes - which reclaims musical instruments in new and fascinating ways. Add the conversation to your calendar here!

 

December 2nd @ 12PM: Steven Riggs, Loft Gallery artist, joins the conversation to tell us more about the works featured in the current exhibition THE HUMAN FACTOR. Add the conversation to your calendar here!

 

December 16th @ 12PM: Lee Ann Lander joins the conversation...more details to come on our website! Add the conversation to your calendar here!

 

Missed a past Conversations and Coffee or want to peruse through our archived collection? Check out our website here where you can find C+Cs dating all the way back to October of 2020!

item.title: The Cultural Arts Center Fundraises, Features New Exhibitions, Gets A Passport and More!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

October 2021 Newsletter

Auction Raises Money For CAC Instructors and Students

We are thrilled to announce that Cultural Art Center and Friends of the Cultural Arts Center's (FCAC) partnership with "Everything But The House" helped raise over $10,000 this fall! Money raised from this auction will be put towards the Professional Development Fund for teachers, as well as several other student scholarships at the Center.

 

We sincerely thank everyone who participated, including the Friends, donors, those who auctioned and all that helped make this auction a reality. Stay tuned for more auction opportunities to come!

Coming Up Next in Our Galleries: Music, Masks, and More!

Exciting things are headed to the Cultural Arts Center's Main Gallery and Loft Gallery this October! 

 

Starting in our Main Gallery, Karin Dahl will merge the visual with the musical in an exhibition titled "Art and Jazz". Pairing paintings with original compositions, Dahl's work invites viewers to consider a conversation between art, music, and how the combination of both creates new meaning.

 

Upstairs in our Loft Gallery, Barbara Vogel and Marjorie "Marge" Bender join together in "Masks", to explore the object of the face mask, and how much the interpretation and symbolism has changed in the last seventeen months. Some masks appear sinister and others playful, while all bring forth more questions than answers.

 

You can see both of these fantastic forthcoming exhibitions when they open Friday, October 8th, 6-8PM. "Art and Jazz" will have accompanying live music with musicians Christian Berg, Brian Cashwell, and Michael Cox beginning at 7PM. If you cannot make the opening, visit us during our normal business hours: Mon. 1-4PM and 7-10PM, Tues.-Thurs. 9-4PM and. 7-10PM, Fri. and Sat. 9-4PM, Sun. CLOSED. 

Have You Picked Up Your Passport?

The Cultural Arts Center is one of the 60+ stops in Columbus Makes Art Passport happening now through October! This program features visual arts exhibitions, gallery shows, theatre, dance, music performances, and more. The best part? It's completely free!

 

You can pick up your passport when you visit us at the Center, and get a unique "stamp" (sticker) along the way! Each stop has an individual and unique sticker created by local artists to fill your passport with - the more you collect, the more cool prizes you can redeem! Prizes include signed artist prints, t-shirts, restaurant gift cards, and tickets to future promotions. Stop by to get yours today and and learn more more about the program here!

The Holidays Are Coming!

The holiday season is just around the corner, and it's never too early to start thinking about something unique to give to someone special!

 

If you're looking for gifts that are creative, handmade and one-of-a-kind, then Columbus Recreation and Parks has it! CAC's very own Created Gift Shop is housed right next to our Main Gallery, while the Golden Hobby Gift Shop, now in its new location, can be found at 549 Franklin Avenue in the Columbus Performing Arts Center!

 

In both shops, you'll find beautiful ceramic works, handmade books, gorgeously crafted jewelry, paintings, drawings and more! All works in Created are made at the Cultural Arts Center by our very own instructors and students, while works in the Golden Hobby Shop are created by senior artists from the local Columbus community.

 

Stop by for a visit and take home something totally unique today!

Created is open during CAC's regular business hours. 

Golden Hobby Shop is open Tues.-Sat. 10AM - 4:30PM and Sun. 1-4PM.

2022-2023 Artist in Residence Applications Opening Soon!

The Cultural Arts Center is excited to announce a new season of our Artist in Residence program! Visit us on our website to stay up to date, and we will have more information to come...stay tuned! 

Class Registration Just Around the Corner...

Have you always wanted to try your hand at painting but weren't sure where to start? Perhaps clay is calling out to you, or jewelry feels exciting and new. There's no better time to start than now!

Our final class session of the year will occur Monday, November 1st - Saturday, December 18th, with registration beginning Saturday, October 23rd, at 8:30AM. You can learn more about our class offerings here, and be sure to create an account to register through the Columbus Recreation and Parks Department’s site here if you haven't done so already.

 

We can't wait to see what you make! What will you create next?

item.title: Cultural Arts Center - Next Session Registration & New Class Offerings!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

New Classes and Registration!

Get ready...registration for our next session of classes is August 28th at 8:30AM! You may register online here or head to the Center in person on Saturday morning. To ensure a speedy registration, make sure to have an account registered with us. Don't have one? Create one here today!

 

In addition to our great slew of class offerings, we have several NEW classes available! 

 

Contemporary Textiles: Mixed Media with Marjaneh Abbasi - This class is designed to help you explore a variety of mixed media techniques including resist techniques using warm/cold wax, crayon, gesso and petroleum jelly. In addition, you will create your own stamps and rubbing plates to create stunning artwork highlighting your unique and expressive voice.

Contemporary Textiles: Monoprinting and Marbling Techniques with Marjaneh Abbasi - This class is designed to help you explore a variety of mixed media techniques featuring Monoprinting and Marbling methods. These techniques include applying paint to smooth surfaces (glass, slick surface) and then making print from the wet paint, next we will make a composition by those pieces with the collage techniques. Through the application of these techniques to collage, we will create stunning artwork that highlights your unique and expressive voice.

Sewing Beyond the Basics with Toia Rivera - Have you always wanted to learn how to sew but are not sure where to start?  This class will teach you how to read the dreaded pattern and adjust it to fit.  You will walk away with the skills you need to be a skilled quilter or garment sewer. Learn to read and understand sewing patterns. Then we will focus on advanced techniques like buttons, zippers, tailoring, and fitting. Class will begin with a basic tote or quilt then move on to garment construction.

Hand Knits by Machine with Toia Rivera - Does machine knitting seem mysterious and a bit daunting? Do you have a knitting machine shoved under your bed or in the back of the closet?  Well, it’s time to pull them out. Learn how to make classic hand knitted patterns by machine. Learn to read and transcribe hand knitted patterns into a machine pattern. Learn how to operate both a double and single bed machine and garment construction, tuck, slip and cable/manipulated stitches. 

 

What will you create next?

item.title: Columbus Cultural Arts Center - August 2021 (CORRECTED)
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Cultural Arts Center Happenings - August 2021

"Everything But The House" Returns to CAC!

This month and next, the Friends of the Cultural Arts Center (FCAC) are teaming up once more with "Everything But The House", a fantastic online auction house.

If you have artwork, furniture, fine jewelry, gift cards, décor, musical instruments, automobiles, or more taking up space in your home, consider donating to our September Online Auction! Proceeds from the auction will be used for the Professional Development Fund as well as student scholarships at the Cultural Arts Center.

Drop off dates and times include: Saturday, August 14th from 10AM-4PM and Sunday, August 15th from 11AM-3PM and will take place in the Center's Main Gallery. More details about the fundraiser can be found on our website, as well more information about the EBTH auction house.

 

Now's the time...start looking around those closets, basements, attics, and garages! 

Sharone Putter's "the workscapes collection" and Philip Sorensen's "Law, Lumber, Stone" Exhibiting Now in Main Gallery

Top: Sharone Putter - W. Main St. and South 2nd St. 
Bottom: Philip Sorensen - Ceci n'est pas un Magritte

Happening now in our Main Gallery, we have not one, but two fantastic exhibitions for you to explore! These include our very own CAC Instructor Sharone Putter, who is presenting "the workscapes collection" - a prolific body of work featuring various monotypes, drawings, and photogravure that explore the world of construction. You can also sign up to attend Putter's closing reception here - it will be taking place Friday, August 20th, from 6-8PM. 

 

Philip Sorensen's life and work as an artist, lawyer, family member, and friend is celebrated in the posthumous exhibition - "Law, Lumber, Stone". Works include a vast range of sculpture both large and small, including wood, marble, concrete, and glass. The exhibition was put together by Sorensen's family, including daughter, Becky Bowers, and curated by artist Michael Kaiser. 

 

You can view these fantastic exhibitions virtually on our website or visit in person during our regular business hours: Mon. 1-4PM and 7-10PM, Tue-Thur. 9AM-4PM and 7-10PM, Fri. + Sat. 9AM-4PM - works will be exhibited until Saturday, August 21st. 

 

In addition to the virtual tours, join us for:

• Instagram Live tour with Putter - watch here. 
• Instagram Live with Bowers - Tuesday, August 10th at noon
• Conversations and Coffee with Bowers 8/12 at noon 
• Conversations and Coffee with Putter 9/23 at noon

More information and links to join can be found on our website.

FCAC Needs Your Help

Did you know that the Cultural Arts Center has a support group?

The Friends of the Cultural Arts Center, a 15 member, not-for-profit organization helps to :

 - Support the programming and activities of the CAC

 - Support and promote instructor professional development

 - Provide student scholarships

 - Manage the gift shop - CREATED 

 - Manage wedding rentals

 - Recruit and work with volunteers

We are seeking individuals who want the Cultural Arts Center to be the best it can be and who have the passion and commitment to help make that happen. At this time, we are especially seeking individuals who have expertise in social media, information technology, law, or finance.

 

The Friends of the Cultural Arts Center is seeking candidates to be active members of the board. If you are interested in serving on the board and learning more about how the Friends work with the CAC administration to make the Center a special place, please contact Franco Ruffini by email at fruffini49@gmail.com or phone (614)747-3013.

Registration for Next Session Coming Soon!

Ready to try your hand at painting, drawing, ceramics, or weaving? Perhaps printmaking, sculpture, jewelry and metals, or enameling catches your interest? Whatever the medium, there is something for everyone at the Cultural Arts Center! 

 

Registration for our fifth session of classes this year will take place on Saturday, August 28th at 8:30AM. You can view class choices and sign up by visiting our website, or, come into the Center the day of registration. Spaces can fill very quickly, so make sure you are logged on or in line at the start time of 8:30AM! It also helps to have an account already created - don't have an account with us? Create one here today. Have questions? Call us at (614)645-7047.

 

What will you create next? 

 

Special Workshops Happening Soon!

Two fantastic workshops are heading to the Cultural Arts Center, including fine art and creative writing!

 

First, join CAC's current Artist in Residence Tiffany Lawson for "Secure the Bag", and explore your imagination through the lens of community and storytelling.

"Come equipped with a brown bag of your choice and various objects. Utilizing mixed media, found objects, color, and texture, you will learn a visual way to express your experiences. Focusing on nature, wellness, and creativity, learn to secure your bag."

This workshop will take place Saturday, August 21st from 1:00PM - 3:00PM and is free to sign up at the front desk! ***Please note that online registration will require a $2 servicing fee.***

Space is limited to first 12 participants that sign up. Register here today!

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

 

Secondly, join artist and writer Mimi Chenfeld for "It's Always the Write Time" a day of creative writing!

"Starting with warm-up exercises, loosening ideas for writers of all levels, all genres, or undecideds! Just as our bodies need to be flexible and strong before we can choreograph dances, we need to strengthen our freedom of spirit, openness, flexibility, courage, and willingness to be playful and enjoy the PROCESS of creativity and the written word! This will be an amazing process full of surprises and open doors welcoming exciting ideas. Bring a lunch and water bottle, lots of paper and pens."

Two sessions remain for this workshop, including Saturday, September 25th and Saturday October 9th, and will take place 9:30AM - 3:30PM. The cost is $30. Register here today!

Just as our bodies need to be flexible and strong before we can choreograph dances, we need to strengthen our freedom of spirit, openness, flexibility, courage, and willingness to be playful and enjoy the PROCESS of creativity and the written word! This will be an amazing process full of surprises and open doors welcoming exciting ideas. Bring a lunch and water bottle, lots of paper and pens."

Two sessions remain for this workshop, including Saturday, September 25th and Saturday October 9th, and will take place 9:30AM - 3:30PM. The cost is $30. Register here today!

item.title: Creative Campus Survey, Class Registration, Summer Workshops, and More!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

Take Our Creative Campus Survey!

The City of Columbus is currently developing a new Creative Campus in Olde Towne East, which will provide creative programming and wellness activities for all community members. 

In addition to housing many of the popular programs from the Martin Janis Community Senior Center and Golden Hobby Shop, there is an opportunity to offer new programs and amenities in this space. Your feedback will help shape what programs and amenities will be included within the building and on the surrounding greenspace.

Visit the Near East Side Creative Campus Information Page to complete this survey today!

 

Workshops Coming This Summer

We have many exciting workshops coming this summer to the Cultural Arts Center, including Surface Design, Cartoneria Mexicana (or paper mâché) and Chakra Bracelet Making!

 

Join Leticia Vazquez Smith (pictured) for a fun filled "How To Make Cartoneria AKA Paper Mâché" on Saturday, June 19th, from 10AM - 1PM. Participants will learn the history of “Cartoneria Mexicana” also known as Paper Mâché, as well as the objects that are made using this technique and their importance to Mexican culture. Other items covered will include glue making, best paper practices, mold techniques, and more. The cost is $25.

 

On the same day, Darsy Amaya will also be leading the workshop "Color Your Life" where participants will be introduced to the seven Chakras and their gemstones through the creation of a handmade bracelet. This bracelet can also be used as a meditation tool, with a focus on visualizing color and repeated affirmations. The workshop will take place 10AM - 12PM and the cost is $20. 

 

You can also join CAC instructor Marjaneh Abbasi for "Surface Design: Methods and Techniques of Creativity" in July! Let your imagination run wild in this two day workshop designed for students to explore many easy and fun mixed media techniques on fabric. Applications presented in this workshop involve the liberal use of paint, ink, sewing, collage and more on a surface of your choice. Supplies will be provided to students along with a materials list, and the cost is $95. 

 

Visit our website to learn more information and sign up today! 

 

FINAL WEEK for Main & Loft Gallery Exhibitions!

This week is the last week to see our Main Gallery and Loft Gallery exhibitions!

Our Main Gallery is currently featuring the Columbus Ohio Watercolor Society's "Spring Exhibition" with more than thirty beautiful works, all in the medium of watercolor.  

Upstairs in our Loft Gallery, artist Marvin Daniels is featuring the exhibition "Transitions" (pictured), which includes painting, ceramics, and mixed media all in a vast array of playful to serious study. 

 

You can catch these two incredible exhibitions now until Saturday, May 29th! Sign up to register for a time to visit on our website, and be sure to stay tuned for more art coming soon!

 

Masks STILL REQUIRED at Cultural Arts Center

To mask or not to mask...the question on everyone's mind! 

At this point, there have been no changes to our COVID-19 Safety Protocols. CRPD is working with Columbus Public health to determine how Governor Mike DeWine's announcement last week may or may not change these protocols. 

All City of Columbus locations still require the public and employees to wear masks in our facilities. Therefore, when visiting the Cultural Arts Center and/or taking a class, wearing a mask is required at all times until further notice. 

 

We expect to receive updated guidelines in the near future. Please continue adhering to the protocols already in place until further notice. 

 

Illustrations by German artist Steffen Kraft.

 

Session 4 Registration Coming Soon!

Beginning Saturday, June 12th you can register for session 4 of classes here at the Cultural Arts Center! Links will go live at 8:30AM sharp, so be sure to log on a few minutes early if registering online. You may also register in person at the Center. 

 

This session will begin after our summer break, starting July 12th and running through September 4th, 2021.

item.description:

Class Registration Begins Saturday, February 20th

 

Classes To Return Monday, March 1st

Classes are set to return once more to the Cultural Arts Center on Monday, March 1st! Class registration takes place this Saturday, February 20th, at the Center as well as on our website. Registration both in person and online begins promptly at 8:30am. With classes ranging from Book Arts to Ceramics, Copper Enameling to Watercolor Painting, there is surely something for everyone!

As a reminder, Covid-19 safety protocols are still in place at the Cultural Arts Center, including mask wearing, the practice of social distancing, frequent hand sanitizing/washing, and one-way travel in and out of the building. This applies to all visitors and students both vaccinated and awaiting vaccine. 

You may view classes and register beginning this Saturday here.

Art Returns to the Main Gallery with "Ekphrastic Fantastic"

 

New Call-and-Response Work On Exhibit Now

Currently featured in our Main Gallery is the exhibition "Ekphrastic Fantastic" -  comprising of over seventy artists and works of art! In a call-and-response style, participants were tasked with responding to an image given at random from the Cultural Arts Center. Images ranged from works of art found throughout the Center to various textures, as well as architectural features both inside and out. Artists then had three weeks to create a new work of art reacting to the given random image, taking into consideration the colors, shapes, feelings, and more. 

The results? Truly fantastic!

Come see for yourself today by signing up on our website for a visit. 

 

Residency Opportunity at the Cultural Arts Center!

 

The Cultural Arts Center celebrates the launch of its ARTIST-in-RESIDENCE [AiR] program with an OPEN CALL for both ARTISTS & PANELISTS! The [AiR] program focuses on three main pillars: NATURE, WELLNESS, and CREATIVITY. Proposed projects by applicants who focus on one or more of these three pillars will be considered for funding. Diversity and Inclusion is a core focus of the City of Columbus and the Cultural Arts Center. 

 

Several residency highlights include:

• 760 square foot, lockable studio space at the Cultural Arts Center located on the second floor (non-live-in, non-sound-proof, accessible by elevator)

• community engagement sessions, both virtual and/or live such as "Conversations & Coffee"

• access to multidisciplinary experts and creative network for critical discourse

• scheduled exhibition/performance opportunities at the conclusion of [AiR]

•  $1400 stipend

 

Visit our website to  learn more about this exciting residency opportunity, to apply for the residency,  or to learn about becoming one of our selection panelists.
